extracted.intended_audience: principal investigators, postdoctoral fellows, and institutional grant administrators applying for or receiving Simons Foundation (SF) or Simons Foundation International (SFI) awards
extracted.subtask_description: Policies and procedures governing administration, allowable uses, reporting, compliance, and closeout for grants and fellowships awarded by the Simons Foundation and Simons Foundation International. Targets requirements for investigators and institutional officials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability and compliance with laws
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators and their institutions must also abide by all applicable laws, statutes and regulations, including those governing the conduct of research on humans or animals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These Foundation policies apply to recipients of all awards administered by the Foundation; investigators/institutions must follow additional applicable laws and regulations at all times.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award letter precedence
rubrics_metrics.description: If any discrepancies exist between the award letter and these policies, the award letter prevails.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always follow the specific terms of the individual award letter when it conflicts with general policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy and data processing consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants and grantees consent to the collection and processing of personal information by the Foundation and its affiliates; when award is from SFI, consent includes transfer between SFI and SF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to SF and SFI privacy policies for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grantee Code of Conduct requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Grantee institutions must maintain an environment free of discrimination, harassment and retaliation; actively promote professional codes of conduct; ensure personnel understand applicable laws and policies; provide accessible reporting with protection from retaliation; respond promptly and investigate reports thoroughly; and support highest ethical standards, strictly prohibiting Research Misconduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All Personnel must comply with this Grantee Code of Conduct. Institutions should implement and adhere to policies and procedures consistent with this Code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of Determinations relating to Prohibited Conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Grantee institutions must provide notice to the Foundation, within ten (10) business days, of any Determination relating to Prohibited Conduct involving Personnel, unless prohibited by law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices should be submitted through the Foundation’s secure portal. The Foundation will maintain confidentiality to the extent required by law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual reporting pathway for Prohibited Conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals should report any Prohibited Conduct that impacts a grant to designated persons at their institution; if the institution does not address the report, the individual may contact the Foundation through its secure portal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If contacted, the Foundation may follow up with the institution to confirm that the grant is being performed consistently with the Grantee Code of Conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foundation review and right to suspend/terminate following Determination
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation will review Determinations and consider the impact on grant performance, and reserves the right to suspend or terminate any grant at any time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Foundation's decisions may consider the institution's response and the effect on the project; suspension/termination authority is retained by SF/SFI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defined terms: Determination, Personnel, Prohibited Conduct, Research Misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions provided for Determination, Personnel, Prohibited Conduct, Research Misconduct (fabrication/falsification/plagiarism; excludes honest errors, differences of opinion or disputes about authorship).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these definitions when interpreting obligations and reporting requirements under the Grantee Code of Conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required use of online grants management systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal Investigators, postdoctoral fellows, Authorized Institution Officials, Signing Officials, Financial Officers and contact delegates must use proposalCENTRAL (pC) and/or Simons Award Manager (SAM) for submitting electronically signed award letters, Progress Reports, Financial Statements and other documents; hard copies will not be accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All required documentation must be submitted through pC and/or SAM; pC records will be migrated to SAM. See SAM FAQ for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution Profile maintenance in SAM
rubrics_metrics.description: Each institution that applies for funding or receives an award must maintain an Institution Profile in SAM including a comprehensive list of all active AIOs, contact delegates, SOs and FOs, and banking details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anyone from the institution can set up a SAM account, but only an AIO or approved contact delegate can manage the Institution Profile. Each institution must have at least two certified AIOs to receive payments. Institutions are responsible for keeping profiles up-to-date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contacts & User Access management
rubrics_metrics.description: Each award includes institution contacts in the Contacts & Personnel section; applicants are strongly recommended to provide both pre- and post-award SOs and FOs during application; users with application access can add/remove personnel in SAM; Foundation manages contacts for awards in proposalCENTRAL via email requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To add/remove project personnel use the Contacts & Personnel section's Add/Modify button; for pC changes email [email protected].

rubrics_metrics.name: User profile modification responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Foundation grants administration staff cannot modify user profiles; users must update their own profile information (title, address, phone, email) within their user profile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institution and users are responsible for keeping SAM accounts current.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shared user account rules
rubrics_metrics.description: If an institution allows multiple SOs and FOs to access awards using a shared user account/email, the AIO or Contacts Delegate must certify the authority of all users; only institution administrators, FOs and/or SOs can register a shared email; naming convention requires first name = institution and last name = 'Shared Account'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Role(s) selected when creating the shared account determine authorized tasks. Shared email addresses may not be registered with an AIO or contact delegate role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic signatures acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: The grantee institution consents to transact business using electronic communications and to utilize electronic signatures; electronically signed documents are deemed to have the same legal effect as original executed copies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If e-signatures are not legally binding in the grantee's jurisdiction, the Foundation will accept a PDF of a signed document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-U.S. award equivalency requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: For grants outside the U.S., the Foundation generally requires that an organization be the equivalent of a U.S. public charity (501(c)(3) + 509(a)(1),(2) or (3)) or complete an equivalency determination via NGOsource; costs of determination paid by the Foundation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approval lasts two years from provided fiscal documents; failure to comply results in termination of awards. Institutions already approved may still be required to submit paperwork if approved period expires midaward. Grantees are responsible for eligibility of subcontracts. SF/SFI do not fund institutions in China (including Hong Kong) or their fiscal sponsors/agents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of funds limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Grant funds and income earned on those funds may be spent only for charitable, religious, scientific, literary or educational purposes and only for the purposes stated in the award letter, substantially in accordance with the submitted budget; no substantial changes without prior written approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grantees with subcontracts must enter agreements consistent with grant terms and Foundation policies. Grant funds must be maintained in a separate account dedicated to the charitable purposes (physically separate bank account or separate bookkeeping account). Financial records must be maintained for at least four years after funds are fully expended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repayment of misused or unexpended funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Grantees will repay any portion of the amount granted that is not used for the purposes of the grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to use funds as required may require reimbursement and can affect future funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited uses of funds (IRC-based restrictions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Grantees agree not to use grant funds for: propaganda/lobbying to influence legislation (IRC 4945(d)(1)); support of candidate/party or voter registration drives (IRC 4945(d)(2)); grants to individuals unless meeting IRC 4945(g); grants to organizations not complying with 4945(d)(4); activities not charitable under section 170(c)(2)(B) of the IRC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grantees must ensure activities and subgrants comply with U.S. tax law restrictions; consult Foundation when in doubt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anti‑terrorism compliance and certifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Grantees must use grant funds in compliance with U.S. laws and regulations including Export Administration Regulations, Executive Order 13224, Global Terrorism Sanctions Regulations (31 C.F.R. Part 594) and other anti-terrorism laws; grantee certifies not to knowingly support or transact with terrorists or designated state sponsors of terrorism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grantee also certifies not to distribute award funds directly or indirectly to terrorist organizations or designated state sponsors of terrorism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Earned interest policy
rubrics_metrics.description: If the grantee institution is a 501(c)(3), earned interest up to $5,000 per project may be kept for general operating support; any amount over $5,000 must be returned within sixty (60) days of the grant end date. Non-501(c)(3) institutions must return earned interest within sixty (60) days of the grant end date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track interest earned on grant funds and remit excess amounts timely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value Added Tax (VAT) treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-U.S. taxes charged for purchasing goods or services that a grantee institution is legally required to pay are an allowable expense; if refunded, credits may be used toward the original aims unless stated otherwise in the award letter; credits should not be reported on the Financial Statement. These costs are unallowable for countries where an exemption exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow local tax law and report/handle VAT credits per award terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational assurances for human and animal research
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators and their institutions must have policies and procedures protecting human research participants and animal subjects and follow Animal Welfare Act and NIH guidelines or equivalent regulations for non-U.S. institutions; investigators are responsible for obtaining all ethical approvals required for the research under the grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions must have up-to-date assurances as of the start date and throughout the grant. Grants may not activate without current approvals unless prior written approval is obtained from the Foundation. Contact the Foundation if assurances expire, are revoked, or ethical approvals are suspended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication acknowledgment and machine-readable formats
rubrics_metrics.description: All published research and activities/public communications resulting from Simons-funded projects must carry the specified acknowledgment: 'This work was supported by a grant from the Simons Foundation [Record ID, Principal Investigator’s Initials].' For SFI-funded projects use the SFI wording. Publications must be in machine-readable formats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public communications include abstracts, posters, press releases, and Internet communications. SF/SFI may distribute project information for publicity. Use of SF/SFI logos requires approval by the communications office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press releases, publicity, and approvals
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless stated otherwise in your award letter, press releases or other media communications and Internet-based communications do not require prior written approval, but descriptions of SF/SFI or its work should be approved by SF communications office; prior written approval required for advertisements/marketing publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact SF communications ([email protected]) for approvals. SSC announcements must be approved by SSC staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preprints and Open Access requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: PIs are required to post preprints on recognized servers (e.g., arXiv, bioRxiv, medRxiv) at the same time as (or before) submission to a peer-reviewed journal and to publish under Open Access licenses, which are allowable budget costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include open access costs in budgets where appropriate; follow SFARI-specific publication guidelines if SFARI-funded or using SFARI resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: ORCID iD requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal Investigators are required to provide their ORCID iD as part of the application process. Any research project personnel whose salary/stipend is supported by the project must have an ORCID iD (including PIs, Co-Investigators, collaborators, postdocs, graduate students, etc.). ORCID iDs will be collected as part of the annual Progress Report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all supported personnel obtain and provide ORCID iDs during application and progress reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual property stance
rubrics_metrics.description: Neither SF nor SFI wishes to participate in commercialization of any intellectual property resulting from a grant; SF/SFI reserve the right to release a summary of findings within a reasonable period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan for IP management with your institution and inform the Foundation of any relevant constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Data and Materials Sharing Plan requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: PIs are required to have a Research Data and Materials Sharing Plan prior to receiving a grant. At minimum it must include sufficient methodological detail to reproduce experiments; a plan to make integral Research Data and Materials available to other scientists for research purposes (with listed exceptions); and a plan to make materials available at the end of the grant (with possible earlier sharing after publication).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions include materials that are readily generated from publication info or obtainable from third parties on reasonable terms. PIs may request additional time for implementation post-grant if a manuscript is under review; approval is case-by-case and time-limited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and treatment of integral Research Data and Materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Research Data and Materials are considered integral if necessary to support major claims of a publication or to reproduce/verify research results; such data should be deposited in appropriate public repositories if too large for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repositories should be readily accessible to academic/nonprofit researchers and free of restrictions on projects or field. Human-subjects data sharing must meet protocol and consent terms. If no suitable repository exists, use electronic supplementary materials or other means.

rubrics_metrics.name: Software, source code, and algorithm sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: If a publication announces new software, the source code or an executable file should be made available; if the primary result is a new algorithm, a description of the source code should be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include software/code sharing in the Sharing Plan; consider licensing and repository deposition to facilitate reuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewable reagents and model organism deposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Genetically modified model organisms and primary/genetically modified cell lines developed or used in SF/SFI-funded projects are considered renewable reagents and must be deposited at third-party repositories (e.g., Jackson Laboratory, Drosophila Genomics Resource Center) as specified in the Sharing Plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If legally binding restrictions prevent deposition, PIs and institutions must work with license holders, repositories and Foundation staff to find acceptable solutions (preferably before use of the reagent). Failure to reach a satisfactory solution may affect future funding. At end of grant, PIs must deposit reagents and institution is responsible for transfer; Foundation will pay repository maintenance costs in reasonable cases and may contract for additional costs at its discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Salary and stipend support guidelines — faculty and personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: No salary cap for PIs or faculty; compensation is prorated according to percent effort. No minimum percent effort required for PIs, but expected to participate in Foundation community activities. Postdoctoral research associates must be employees with benefits of the grantee institution; no salary cap. Graduate Research Assistant compensation has no cap but is prorated and should be within department norms; indirect costs may be taken on salaries/stipends but not on tuition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellowship stipends and allowances are outlined in award letters; fellows typically are not treated as employees unless stated. No indirect costs on SF/SFI-funded postdoctoral fellowships unless stated. Stipend/salary supplementation is allowed if fellowship remains main source of support; fellows may not hold another concurrent postdoctoral fellowship unless authorized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Travel expense rules
rubrics_metrics.description: All travel charged to an award must be reasonable, necessary and directly related to the award's scope of work. Travel/accommodation expenses exclusively related to Foundation-organized meetings must be reimbursed outside of award funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan travel budgets accordingly and seek reimbursement channels for Foundation meeting travel when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment ownership and capitalization thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: SF/SFI will own equipment purchased with grant funds with a unit cost of $50,000 or more unless stated otherwise in the award letter; at end of the grant or upon termination SF/SFI reserves the right to cede ownership to the PI’s institution. Equipment with unit cost of $50,000 or less shall be property of the PI’s institution unless stated otherwise in the award letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indirect costs may not be taken on equipment with a unit cost over $10,000. Document equipment purchases and expect Foundation ownership claims for high-value items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research supplies policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation does not require a detailed justification of supplies unless stated otherwise in the award letter. The Foundation reserves the right to purchase and provide some research supplies and approved investigators may access SFARI data and biospecimens through SFARI Base.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult SFARI Base for biospecimen acquisition policies. Use Foundation-provided resources where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect cost policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Indirect costs to the primary institution are limited to 20 percent of direct costs, with exceptions for equipment >$10,000, tuition, and subcontractor costs in excess of $25,000. Primary institution may take indirect costs on the first $25,000 modified total direct costs of each subcontract. Indirect costs paid to a subcontractor may not exceed 20 percent of modified total direct costs paid to the subcontractor. The indirect cost rate is nonnegotiable. No indirect costs on SF/SFI-funded postdoctoral fellowships unless specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget and negotiate subcontracts with these caps in mind; the rate is fixed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment methods and conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: All payments are made in U.S. dollars, disbursed biannually by the end of the first and third quarters unless award letter states otherwise. Payments made via EFT (ACH for U.S., wire for non-U.S.). Payments payable only to institutions; not to individuals. Payment contingent on receipt and approval of electronically signed award letter and completed EFT Form in SAM, and annual certification of EFT payment info.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide accurate EFT information; Foundation will not reimburse exchange-rate fluctuations or bank fees. Payment references include Record ID numeric portion and PI's initial and last name.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withholding, suspension, and termination for reporting noncompliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to provide timely and complete Financial Statements, Progress Reports or other required Deliverables may result in withholding payments, suspension, early termination and/or reimbursement of unexpended funds. If reports are not provided by due dates payments will be withheld; after 42 days grant will be suspended; after 72 days grant may be terminated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payments may also be withheld/suspension/termination for limited progress as determined by the Foundation in its discretion. Resumption requires written approval and a new timeline for reporting progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of unacceptable personnel changes or unapproved project changes
rubrics_metrics.description: A grant may be suspended or terminated if a change in key personnel is deemed unacceptable by the Foundation. Changing the research plan without prior written approval will result in termination and require reimbursement of funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain prior written approval for substantive changes in scope or key personnel changes that could affect project performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required deliverables on termination
rubrics_metrics.description: All early terminations require submission of a Final Progress Report and a Final Financial Statement within thirty (30) days after the effective date of termination. Refunds for unexpended funds will be issued within thirty (30) days of submission and approval of the Final Financial Statement, after withholding noncancelable costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon termination, do not incur new obligations and cancel outstanding obligations where possible; grantee receives credit for properly incurred costs before suspension/termination that are not cancelable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators are expected to share data, results, reagents and other research products developed with grant funds, and to participate in Foundation-hosted workshops, teleconference lab meetings and online tools. Investigators are expected to participate in certain conferences, workshops and symposia organized by the Foundation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Travel and accommodation exclusively related to Foundation meetings will be reimbursed outside award funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant activation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: To accept the award, an electronically signed copy of the award letter is due on or before the start date of the grant in SAM. The award will be terminated without activation if not signed within thirty (30) days of the due date or start date. Grants will not be activated without current human/animal ethical approvals without prior written approval of the Foundation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure award letters are signed timely and necessary approvals are in place before start date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual EFT payment information confirmation
rubrics_metrics.description: EFT payment information must be submitted via an EFT form in SAM and signed/submitted by appropriate AIOs. Annually, two AIOs must confirm EFT payment information. Failure to submit or confirm will result in withholding of funds for all awards at the institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign AIOs to certify EFT info annually and whenever bank details change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Progress report deadlines (annual and final)
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual Progress Reports are due on or before the end of each funding year of the award. Final Progress Reports are due within 120 days of the award end date or within 30 days of termination or transfer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow specified deliverable deadlines in SAM and assign Signing Official authority as required for submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deliverables and authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: A set of named deliverables (e.g., Electronically Signed Copy of Award Letter, Financial Statement, Reallocation of Funds Request, Progress Report, Final Progress Report, Carry Forward Request, No-Cost Extension Request) have specific due dates and must be signed/submitted by designated authorities (Signing Official, Financial Officer, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check award letter and Deliverables section for due dates and appropriate signers; only users assigned to SO or FO roles can sign/submit corresponding deliverables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change of institution process and required documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: With Foundation approval, PIs may transfer their grant to a new institution (domestic/foreign nonprofit or public/private institutions) provided both institutions agree; award cannot be transferred to for-profit organizations. Required from original institution: Transfer Deliverable and Financial Statement due within 30 days of transfer effective date; unexpended funds returned within 30 days following approval. Required from new institution: new application including revised budget signed by SO, confirming PI appointment and institutional support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approval triggers closeout letter to original institution and award letter to new institution. Follow timelines for financial reporting and fund transfers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change of Principal Investigator requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Change of PI is allowed only under rare circumstances and requires a Change of Principal Investigator Deliverable signed by the institution’s Signing Official stating reason, verification of new PI’s eligibility/qualifications/availability, and description of how change affects scope/implementation/timeline; the new PI’s CV/biosketch must be uploaded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide full documentation to support the requested PI change; approval is discretionary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changes in project or key personnel (non-PI) policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes in project personnel or key personnel (other than PI) do not require prior approval. Changes in percent effort of project or key personnel do not require prior approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Update SAM Contacts & Personnel as needed to reflect staffing changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closeout requirements and timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: To close out a grant, grantee must submit a Final Progress Report and a Final Financial Statement due within 120 days of the end date. Unexpended funds must be returned within 30 days following approval of the Financial Statement. Refunds from U.S. institutions via ACH; non-U.S. refunds via international wire transfer. Refunds exceeding requested amount by less than $1 will be rounded and excess not returned. Award closure notification will confirm if SF/SFI will cede or maintain ownership of equipment over $50,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not remit payment for unspent funds until Foundation has approved the Financial Statement and requested a refund. Follow refund methods and deadlines precisely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roles and responsibilities glossary (PI, Co-Investigator, SO, FO, AIO, Contact Delegate)
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions and role-specific responsibilities: PI must hold Ph.D./M.D. or equivalent and a faculty/equivalent position; may be multiple PIs but one spokesperson PI for administrative purposes; Co-Investigator must hold Ph.D./M.D. and be affiliated/employed by applicant/grantee; SO is responsible for legal binding and certifying submissions; FO is responsible for accounting and Financial Statements; AIO legally binds the institution and manages Institution Profile; Contact Delegate manages contacts and approves SOs/FOs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign and certify institutional roles in SAM; ensure SO/FO/AIO understand signing authorities and responsibilities for deliverables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution Profile deliverable requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Institution Profile-related deliverables (EFT Payment Information Web Form(s), Institution Contacts Certification, Primary Institution Official General Email Acknowledgment, Shared pC User Acknowledgment, Primary Institution Official Update, Institution Contact Update) are due at inception and/or annually or as needed and must be signed by Primary Signing Official or Primary Financial Officer or as specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the listed authorities for each deliverable; maintain and update Institution Profile information in SAM per requirements.
